name: Shipped deep-run prompt with standing instructions
description: Builds the real goal prompt, which includes the standing instructions as a required part, and runs it headless with every tool disabled, then has the model judge grade the stated plan. No runtime arm backs it: the standing instructions are text the agent reads and only this evaluation arm exercises them, so the evaluation arm stays selected.
advantages: Closest measured stand-in for what ships, so it is the arm that earns the selection even on a tie. Selected because: TIE, kept by the stated reason: the metric does not separate the standing instructions from the plain in-situ prompt (the pass rates are inside the leaderboard's margin for sampled, model-judged runs and the instructions spend more tokens), so the arm stays because quest_ai_runner/prompts/evolvable_structure.md is what the deep run actually loads (standing deep-run instructions, generated from the skill by scripts/sync_standing_instructions.py), and the arms without it are not what ships
disadvantages: Costs real model calls, spends extra tokens on the instructions, and scores only a described plan, not real edits.

name: In-situ prompt without the instruction layer
description: The same headless, tool-less deep-run path with the standing-instructions layer emptied, so the only difference from the shipped arm is the layer itself. It is a baseline.
advantages: Isolates the effect of the instruction layer cleanly and is cheaper in tokens.
disadvantages: It is not what ships, and the model may already behave well on many scenarios without help.

name: Chat-completion ablation with instructions
description: One plain model call per case with the instruction file as the system prompt, then the judge. It is an ablation that measures the instructions alone, outside the deep-run path.
advantages: Simple and cheap to run, and it separates the instruction text from the surrounding prompt.
disadvantages: A bare chat completion is not the setting the instructions ship in, so it should never be adopted on its own.

name: Chat-completion baseline without instructions
description: One call per case with a generic helpful-assistant system prompt, then the judge, so the gain from the instructions is a measured difference.
advantages: Cheapest comparator and gives a clear zero-instruction reference.
disadvantages: Not representative of the deep run, and a strong model may pass many cases without any help, which makes the gain look small.

name: Rubric-based model judge
description: A cheap-tier model call with tools off receives the scenario, expected behaviour, failure mode and reply, but never the regexes or reference replies, and returns a single JSON verdict. Unparseable output is a fail. No runtime arm backs it: the judge only scores the behavior this repository measures, so the evaluation arm stays selected.
advantages: Grades behaviour in different words, resists vocabulary gaming, and generalises to new cases. Selected because: evaluation/components/esoi_behavior/judge.py (build_judge), used by every judged esoi_behavior arm
disadvantages: Can favour its own phrasing when it is the same model as the replies, costs a call per reply, and is only as good as the case author's rubric.

name: Regex-check floor
description: Passes a reply when every required pattern matches and no forbidden pattern does, with no model call. It is a baseline.
disadvantages: Agrees with the labels almost by construction since the same author wrote both, and it rewards the right words rather than the right action.

description: . Backed at run time by the arm conftest (tests/conftest.py, which keeps the suite offline); this arm measures it and stays selected as the measured one.
advantages: Selected because: CLAUDE.md pre-commit rule: run only the tests your change touches; this collection check is the cheap whole-suite gate

name: Planted-secret evaluation arm
description: Runs the live scanner on text assembled from fragments (so the test file itself is clean), on groups of real repository files, and as a command in a throwaway git repository. No runtime arm in this repository backs it: the scanner is the hub's secret redaction, to which adapters/files_redaction.py adds only the Quest key shape; the evaluation arm stays selected.
advantages: Proves both detection and silence on placeholders against the real scanner, without keeping real secrets anywhere. Selected because: `esoi hygiene` (CLAUDE.md pre-commit step 2, docs/how-to/public-hygiene.md)
disadvantages: Planted cases only cover the shapes someone thought to add.

advantages: Selected because: core/resolve.py resolve() over the declarations beside each implementation and the records (S30)

name: Problem-linked tag list with a check rule and a lookup
description: esoi/tags.csv holds each tag with a one-sentence meaning and the problems it mitigates (problem_ids); solutions carry tags in their tags column; the QAR rule Q1 in scripts/esoi_tags.py (registered by the plugin scripts/esoi_rules.py) fails a tag outside the list, a listed tag with no meaning, with no linked problem or with a linked id that is not a problem record, and a tag used by no solution or by every solution, and prints a note for a tag on one solution. tags_of and solutions_sharing (and the script run as a command) read a solution's tags as its column plus its problem_ids.
advantages: One list as the source of truth; every tag's risk is a problem record that can be read, linked and solved; the lookup uses the links that already exist, so problem ids are never copied.
disadvantages: The rule cannot judge whether a tag mitigates its risk or whether a link already identifies the same solutions; that rests on the back-fill procedure and, later, on the metric. R1 to R4 are recorded in this project, not yet in the library that owns them.
